Trigeminal neuralgia. Selective destruction of pain-bearing nerves is reserved for patients who do not respond to convention- al drug therapy for trigeminal neuralgia (p.9). This may be achieved by the instillation of glycerol among the trigeminal rootlets (percutaneous retrogasserian glycerol rhizolysis).1-5 The efficacy and safety of this procedure have been debated,1,4 but some centres report good long-term results in the majority of pa- tients.5 It has been suggested that variations in viscosity and os- molality may influence results.2 1.
